content.value_statement: Empathy Ledger contributors need fast context for sensitive platform work. This skill gives concise project patterns for tenancy, cultural safety, services, and workflows.
actual_capabilities: Summarizes the Empathy Ledger v2 source tree and key application domains.
Explains OCAP principles, tenant isolation, cultural sensitivity levels, and story ownership checks.
Provides authentication and ownership check patterns for API route reviews.
Lists database domain files, core services, slash commands, and specialized agents.
Identifies when to use the skill during component, endpoint, migration, and compliance work.
limitations: It is a reference guide, not an executable development tool.
It does not include the referenced CLAUDE.md, agent prompts, commands, or database type files.
It does not validate code, run tests, or enforce Supabase policies.
Cultural, legal, and security decisions still need qualified human review.

use_cases.title: Start a Feature Safely
use_cases.description: Review project structure, UI areas, color roles, and cultural sensitivity expectations before creating a new Empathy Ledger screen.

use_cases.title: Plan Data Access
use_cases.description: Use tenancy, RLS, authentication, and story ownership guidance before designing an endpoint or Supabase migration.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Reviews
use_cases.description: Map a change to relevant services, domains, slash commands, and reviewer roles before release planning.

prompt_templates.title: Find the Right Pattern
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner orientation for a new task
prompt_templates.prompt: Use empathy-ledger-dev to orient me before I build [feature]. Summarize the relevant project areas and key constraints.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Use empathy-ledger-dev to plan a React component for [workflow]. Include the relevant UI area, color role, and cultural sensitivity concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Endpoint
prompt_templates.prompt: Use empathy-ledger-dev to review this endpoint idea: [description]. Check authentication, tenant isolation, story ownership, and consent concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Cross-Domain Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Use empathy-ledger-dev to plan [feature] across database domains, services, review roles, cultural protocols, testing, and release risks.

output_examples.input: I need a Story Vault view for elder approvals.
output_examples.output: The skill points to vault and cultural components, the sage color role, high sensitivity content, and elder approval requirements.

output_examples.input: I am adding an API route for story sharing.
output_examples.output: The skill highlights authentication, tenant isolation, ownership checks, DistributionService, EmbedService, and no external sharing for sacred stories.

output_examples.input: I need a release review checklist for a consent change.
output_examples.output: The skill directs attention to consent and legal domains, GDPR service behavior, audit logging, cultural review, security review, and ownership controls.

best_practices: Pair this skill with current repository files before editing a feature.
Check tenant isolation and story ownership before adding data access.
Apply cultural sensitivity rules early, then request human review for sacred content workflows.
anti_patterns: Do not treat the reference as a complete specification for missing files.
Do not bypass RLS, tenant checks, or ownership checks for speed.
Do not make cultural protocol decisions without community or elder review.

faq.question: Does this skill run commands?
faq.answer: No. It only provides reference guidance and examples for Empathy Ledger development work.

faq.question: Is this skill specific to Empathy Ledger v2?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance names Empathy Ledger v2 folders, domains, services, and workflows.

faq.question: Does it include the referenced agent or command files?
faq.answer: No. It references those files, but this package only includes SKILL.md.

faq.question: Can it replace security review?
faq.answer: No. It helps identify expected checks, but qualified reviewers must assess real code changes.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should I verify before publishing changes?
faq.answer: Verify tenant isolation, story ownership, consent rules, cultural sensitivity handling, tests, and human review requirements.
